author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수만 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 우리나라의 해안과 하구에서 흔히 보이는 나그네새로, 주로 호수나 하천 같은 물가에 산다. 이동할 때는 30~100마리씩 무리를 지어 움직이며, 작은 물고기와 곤충, 갑각류를 먹는다. 번식지에서는 호수나 하천의 갈대·왕골 사이에 마른 풀줄기를 높이 쌓아 화산 모양 둥지를 무리 지어 짓고, 알을 2~3개 낳는다. 시베리아 동부, 캄차카, 사할린, 쿠릴 열도 등지에서 번식하고 아프리카 동부 열대, 동남아시아, 오스트레일리아 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: pale grey scapulars, back and rump

art.subject: Common Tern (Sterna hirundo), East Asian subspecies longipennis, adult in breeding plumage as seen on Korean coasts on spring passage (May): solid black cap from the bill base through the eye to the nape; white cheeks and throat forming a clean white band below the cap; scapulars, back, rump and upperwings pale grey, outer primaries darker grey; breast and belly washed pale grey, clearly greyer than the white cheek band; undertail coverts white; tail white, deeply forked with long outer streamers. Bill black. Dark eye. Short dark reddish-brown legs.
art.pose: flying over the water with a small migrating flock
art.scene: Korean estuary where a river meets the sea, tidal channels and sandbars; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view perched on a post: black cap from forehead to nape, white cheeks and throat, pale grey back and wings, breast and belly washed pale grey below the white cheek band, white undertail coverts, forked tail reaching about the wingtips, black bill, short dark legs

adult in flight seen from below, head, body and tail in one line: pale grey breast and belly, white undertail coverts and axillaries, pale underwing with a dark trailing edge to the outer primaries, deeply forked white tail, black bill
art.build: Medium-sized, slender tern, 35.5cm including the tail streamers, slimmer and much lighter than a Black-headed Gull; long, narrow, pointed wings and a deeply forked tail. Bill straight and sharply pointed, about as long as the head. Legs short, dark reddish-brown. At rest the tail streamers reach about the wingtips, not beyond. In flight from above pale grey wings with a darker grey wedge on the outer primaries; from below a dark trailing edge to the outer primaries. Hovers and plunge-dives for small fish.
avoid: Do not paint a bright orange-red bill; East Asian Common Terns (longipennis) have a blackish bill.
Do not paint a white forehead with a yellow bill — that is Little Tern (Sternula albifrons).
Do not paint tail streamers projecting far beyond the wingtips at rest.
Do not paint a shaggy crest (crested terns).
